There are 119 such integers. I counted them by hand and did not run code to cross-check.

**Reducing the conditions.**
- n ≡ 1 (mod 5) means the last digit is 1 or 6. Condition 1 rules out a digit 1, so n ends in 6.
- Any n from 10000 to 19999 starts with 1, and 20000 ends in 0, so n has 4 digits.
- Any n from 1633 to 1999 also starts with 1. So n lies in 2048..9998 (the smallest power of two above those excluded numbers), and n = 2m with m having exactly 5 one-bits and m ≡ 3 (mod 5).

**Enumeration.** I split by the top bit of m and used the powers of 2 mod 5, which cycle through 1, 2, 4, 3. For each split I listed the valid bit sets whose weights sum to the required residue. I then computed n = 2m for each and discarded any n containing the digit 1.

| Top bit of m | Bit sets with the right residue | Survive the digit-1 check |
|---|---|---|
| 2¹² (n from 8192) | 38, of which 37 give n ≤ 9998 | 32 |
| 2¹¹ (n from 4096) | 74 | 55 |
| 2¹⁰ (n from 2048) | 42 | 32 |

The total is 32 + 55 + 32 = 119.

As a spot check, 2456 = 2048+256+128+16+8 has 5 one-bits, 2456 mod 5 = 1, and it has no digit 1, so it is counted.

ANSWER: 119
